resource.title: A Phase III, Randomised, Double-blind, Two-arm Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Treatment With CHF10196 Tablets (Florensocatib) Compared With Placebo for up to 78 Weeks, Followed by an Open-label Extension, in Male and Female Participants 12 to 85 Years of Age With Bronchiectasis
resource.description:
This study aims to find out whether the tablet CHF10196 is safe and effective for people with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, a long-term lung disease that causes widened airways, mucus buildup, infections, and flare ups of symptoms. The main goal is to see whether CHF10196 can reduce the number of lung flareups each year compared with placebo. The study will also assess whether it can improve lung function, quality of life, and overall safety.

The study has two phases. In the first phase, participants receive either CHF10196 tablets or placebo without knowing which one they are taking. In the second phase, all participants receive CHF10196 so its long-term safety can be further studied. Adults aged 18 to 85 years and adolescents aged 12 to under 18 years can take part, while continuing their usual stable bronchiectasis treatment.

Up to about 2.5 years of participation are planned. Around 904 participants will be enrolled, with regular clinic visits and phone check ins. In the first phase, participants take either CHF10196 or inactive tablets once daily; in the second phase, everyone takes CHF10196 once daily. Temporary treatment interruptions are allowed if needed, and participants who stop treatment early may still continue study visits, depending on the study phase.

extension.valueMarkdown:
This study looks at whether the tablet CHF10196 is safe and works well for people with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis. This is a long-term lung disease that can make the airways wider, cause mucus to build up, and lead to infections and symptom flare-ups.

The main goal is to see whether CHF10196 lowers the number of lung flare-ups each year compared with a placebo, which is a tablet with no active medicine. The study also checks whether CHF10196 improves lung function, quality of life, and overall safety.

The study has two phases. In the first phase, people take either CHF10196 tablets or placebo tablets. Chance decides which one you get, and you do not know which one you are taking. In the second phase, everyone takes CHF10196 so researchers can learn more about its long-term safety.

Adults aged 18 to 85 years and adolescents aged 12 to under 18 years can join. You keep taking your usual stable bronchiectasis treatment during the study.

Up to about 2.5 years of participation are planned. Around 904 people will take part. You will have regular clinic visits and phone check-ins. In the first phase, you take either CHF10196 or inactive tablets once daily. In the second phase, everyone takes CHF10196 once daily. Temporary breaks in treatment are allowed if needed. If you stop treatment early, you may still continue study visits, depending on the study phase
